subject: Performance & data-residency follow-up — latency/throughput targets and regional routing
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@canyonhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@canyonhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood performance discussion + data residency constraints

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good overview from your side. A few concrete points from our internal review that we need to lock down before we can move to procurement:

- Latency targets: our product team is aiming for p95 <= 150ms for short-text responses (typical prompt size ~30 tokens) and p99 <= 400ms for peak bursts. Streaming use-cases (live transcription to model) need sub-200ms first-token latency ideally.
- Throughput/concurrency: steady-state 250 qps per region with bursts to 800 qps for transactional windows; concurrent streams expected ~120 active connections during peaks.
- Model behavior: we care about consistent tail latency for safety-critical prompts; regressions are a showstopper.
- Regional routing & residency: EU traffic that contains patient data (PHI) must remain within EU boundaries. APAC footprint is a requirement for future rollout — for now US + EU routing rules.
- Security/compliance: procurement will request SOC2 evidence and an explanation of where logs/telemetry are stored and for how long.

Can you put together a short note confirming (a) whether Redwood can meet the latency/throughput targets with dedicated capacity or hybrid routing, (b) tradeoffs for streaming vs batch inference, and (c) a proposed minimal topology for US/EU split that enforces residency for PHI?

If possible we’d like a ballpark cost delta between hosted vs dedicated for this profile — procurement will need that to budget.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Platform
Canyon Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@canyonhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood performance discussion + data residency constraints

Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Aditya, Grace, and Priyom to validate the feasibility and give us numbers. High level answers up front: yes, we can design for your targets with a combination of dedicated capacity and regional topology controls. Below are the proposed starting assumptions and next steps.

Summary answers (short):
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms (short responses) is achievable with dedicated pools in-region + warmed KV cache; p99 sub-400ms for the same profile is feasible with properly sized pre-warmed instances and low-concurrency batching.
- Throughput/Concurrency: a per-region dedicated pool sized for steady 250 qps with autoscale headroom to 800 qps and warm concurrency slots for ~150 concurrent streams is the recommended baseline.
- Streaming: use lightweight streaming model variant + lower-precision quantization for first-token latency; maintain a high-accuracy variant for final generation.
- Data residency: deploy EU-only inference with strict egress controls and route PHI-labeled requests to EU nodes. Logs/metrics can be configured to redact PHI and store telemetry in-region or in the RBAC'd control plane depending on contract.

Proposed next steps:
1) Aditya to provide a concise perf matrix (p95/p99 vs model size, quantization, batch) for short prompt/streaming scenarios (deliverable: latency_benchmark_matrix.csv).
2) Grace to sketch a minimal regional topology diagram and routing policy (US primary, EU for PHI; APAC as future).
3) Priyom to outline a canary/rollout plan and required SLAs for the dedicated pool.
4) Karthik to produce a mutual action plan with owners and a budget range for procurement.

Can you confirm whether the PHI constraints mean we should treat all requests with the patient_id field as PHI — i.e., route on that label? If so we’ll include field-based routing in the topology.

I’ll capture the MAP and share a doc + cost band this week. Proposed joint working session on Mon 29 Sep — does that work for you (we’ll invite Infra and your procurement team)?

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwoodinference.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 10:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood performance discussion + data residency constraints

Karthik / team — quick tech write-up to back up the summary above. Dropping the numbers we typically see and the tradeoffs. Attaching a small perf matrix (latency_benchmark_matrix.csv) that includes representative p50/p95/p99 samples for short prompts (30 tokens) across a couple model configs.

Key points:
- Baseline: for 30-token prompts on a 13B open model (quantized to 4-bit), in-region dedicated GPU pool with continuous batching yields p95 ~ 120–160ms, p99 ~ 300–420ms depending on burst patterns and cache hit rate.
- Streaming first-token: with our streaming-optimized variant and pre-warmed fast path, first-token p50 ~ 40–70ms, p95 ~ 120–190ms. Getting sub-200ms first-token consistently requires smaller models for the first-pass or using a reduced-context model for head-of-session.
- Throughput: a single high-density GPU node (x4 GPUs) with concurrency tuned can sustain ~200–300 qps for short responses; scale horizontally for the 800-qps burst headroom. Autoscale + pre-warm ramp is critical to avoid degraded tails.
- Concurrency / Streams: for ~120 concurrent streams, we recommend reserving warm concurrency slots (idle instances) rather than cold-starting. Reservation reduces unit cost slightly but prevents tail latency spikes.
- Residency enforcement: tag requests at the edge (a header or token claiming PHI), route by policy to EU-only clusters; ensure streaming blobs and temp KV cache are pinned to EU storage.

Tradeoffs and quick recommendations:
- Hosted (shared) + routing: cheaper to start, but tail latency and strict PHI compliance are harder to guarantee.
- Dedicated per-region: higher baseline cost, predictable latency, straightforward PHI isolation.
- Hybrid: route PHI to dedicated EU pool, non-PHI to hosted US pool — lowers cost and satisfies residency.

I’ve attached the CSV with raw samples; Grace/ Priyom feel free to call out anything to add before we share this with the customer.

Attachment: latency_benchmark_matrix.csv (CSV, 14 KB) — includes p50/p95/p99 samples and config notes.

—Aditya
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Procurement will need a ballpark monthly cost range for both (A) hosted + routing hybrid and (B) dedicated per-region. If you can give us a delta (e.g., +X% for dedicated vs hosted) that’s sufficient for budgeting.

We’re available for the working session on Mon 29 Sep at 10:00am PT — I’ve included procurement on the thread. Please send a calendar invite and any pre-reads.

- Dedicated per-region (US + EU dedicated pools): ~ +80–120% vs standard hosted (predictable latency and strict residency).
